about: The stated ICP and strategy say enterprise; every paying customer is a one-to-five person business. The contradiction must reach the founder as two positions, never averaged away, and no team may quietly resolve it.

planted.issue: The ICP is in-house legal teams at 500+ employee companies, but all 14 paying customers have 1 to 5 employees. Reported above everything else, as a contradiction with the recorded decision to sell to enterprise first, without choosing a side.
'Enterprise-grade ... with full audit trails' is contradicted by the product itself: single-user accounts, no SSO, no audit log.
The ICP evidence is two discovery calls, with no enterprise customer or pilot: it is assumed, not evidenced.
Runway on September net burn is about 4.9 months ($60,000 / $12,294), under six months and well below the 9 months in the brain; it should lead the response.
Enterprise marketing (LinkedIn legal-operations ads at $1,500 a month and the $4,000 LegalTech Summit booth) has produced no enterprise customer or pilot; all revenue is the $29 Solo plan.
The decision 'sell to enterprise legal teams first' should be revisited if no enterprise pilot is signed by 2026-09-30, and none is. Surfaced to the founder, not decided by the team.

The formal, corporate identity is aimed at enterprise legal teams while every paying customer is a founder, freelancer or small agency; flagged as a mismatch tied to the ICP and positioning, and raised rather than resolved.
Declines to write the tagline: wording belongs to Growth. Returns that part to the Orchestrator instead of writing one.
Names the question underneath SSO and audit logs and points out that no paying customer is an enterprise (all are 1 to 5 people), so the feature serves a customer the company does not have yet.
Estimates in founder-hours with assumptions and checks them against 2 x 35 = 70 founder-hours; recommends the thinnest scope or says what makes it insufficient.
